text:
nina: Heads-up: our edge sample started showing type regressions after we switched to a single esbuild bundle. Generics like `client.run<MyShape>()` are inferred as `any` in consumers. Runtime works fine but TS types are busted. Anyone have quick ideas?

 dave: Oof. That usually means an overload or exported type got widened somewhere. Can you share the callsite + the lib .d.ts snippets?

 nina: Sure — callsite:
 ```ts
 const result = await client.run<{ id: string }>({ model: 'rwd-edge', prompt: 'hey' });
 // expecting result.id to be string, TS reports any after build
 ```
 and the SDK types in node_modules look like:
 ```ts
 run<T>(opts: RunOpts & { format: 'parsed' }): Promise<T>
 run(opts: RunOpts): Promise<any>
 ```

 pat: That fallback `Promise<any>` will cause inference to collapse in ambiguous resolution cases. If tsc can't guarantee the first overload across module boundaries it picks the broader signature.

 nina: We also had `skipLibCheck: true` in the edge sample tsconfig to speed CI. I disabled it locally and got a ton of declaration mismatch errors inside the SDK. Not sure how to proceed.

 dave: Two pragmatic fixes: 1) make the fallback generic `run<T = any>(opts: RunOpts): Promise<T>` so callers still get inference; or 2) prefer `Promise<unknown>` for the fallback and expose a small narrow helper like `as<T>(v: unknown): T` for common cases. I prefer unknown for public types.

 pat: Also audit tsconfig differences. For edge/esbuild we should use `module: 'ESNext'` + `moduleResolution: 'bundler'` and not `node16` or `nodenext`. Mismatch in moduleResolution can lead to different .d.ts being picked by the compiler.

 qa-bot: CI: samples/edge-ts types job failed — samples/edge-ts/src/app.ts: line 18 "Type 'any' is not assignable to type '{ id: string }'". More details: https://ci.internal/9001/jobs/22

 nina: Good catch. I'll try swapping the fallback to `unknown` and add a TS test (tsd) that asserts `run<{ id: string }>` infers correctly. Also will stop skipping lib checks in sample CI so these surface early.

 dave: If you change `any` -> `unknown` in public types, include migration notes. It will cause some user code to require explicit narrowing. Also add a dtsnapshot that validates the published `dist/index.d.ts` to catch packaging transforms that flatten overloads.

 pat: Another hidden gotcha: esModuleInterop + allowSyntheticDefaultImports flips import shapes. If published types use `export =` but consumers import as default the shape might differ leading TS to select different overloads. Make sure package.json `types` points to the single canonical d.ts and that both ESM and CJS builds reference compatible types.

 pkg-bot: opened issue #599: "edge sample: bundling + tsconfig mismatch causing generic inference to widen" assigned to nina.

 nina: I'll open a small PR with three things: 1) change fallback to `Promise<unknown>` + helper narrower, 2) add tsd test for generic inference, 3) update samples/edge-ts/tsconfig.json to `moduleResolution: 'bundler'` and remove `skipLibCheck` in CI. Tagging dave/pat for review.

 dave: Also consider adding a short note in samples/README about recommended tsconfig per runtime (edge vs node) so new contributors don't accidentally match the wrong resolution.

 pat: Agreed. Thanks for chasing this down, nina. Small typing regressions like this are painful but worth the extra test coverage.

 qa-bot: rerun: types job passed after temporary pin to previous SDK types (jobs/22).

 nina: will include changelog blurb if anything user-visible changes. Thanks all :thumbsup:
